description: Build an HTTP Basic auth header from user and password, or decode one: header takes a whole Authorization: Basic … line, a Basic … value or the bare base64. mode is decode when header is given and build otherwise. The result shows the user and password with their bytes, and the header. Example: user Aladdin, password open sesame. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

header.description: What to decode: an Authorization: Basic … line, a Basic … value or the bare base64.

mode.description: build an HTTP Basic auth header from user and password, or decode header; omitted, it is decode when header is given and build otherwise.

password.description: The password to build the header from, sent as UTF-8.

user.description: The user name to build the header from; it can't contain ':'.

name: cipher_basic_auth
title: HTTP Basic auth header

description: Decode X.509 certificates and signing requests from PEM, or DER as base64 or hex: subject and SANs, validity, issuer, key, usages and SHA-256 fingerprints. Several certificates are checked as a chain, for order and each signature; expiry, SHA-1 and CN-only certificates are flagged, and key says which certificate a public or private key belongs to. now sets the time validity is judged at. Example: cert -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----… Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

cert.description: Certificates and signing requests to decode, as PEM (several are checked as a chain), or DER as base64 or hex; may be left out when cert_file is uploaded.

key.description: A public or private key (PEM, JWK or an OpenSSH line) to match against the certificates and requests, naming the one it belongs to.

now.description: Unix time in seconds to use as the current time, e.g. 1700000000; omit it for the real clock.

name: cipher_cert
title: Decode certificates

description: Show the same bytes as UTF-8 text, hex, base64, base64url and base32: text is read per from (utf8 by default), and the base64 variant it was in is named. A character that isn't valid in the encoding is pointed at by its offset. Use it to see what a base64 or hex value holds, or to re-encode bytes. Example: text aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=, from base64. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

from.description: How text is written: utf8 (as typed), hex, base64 (either alphabet, padded or not), base64url or base32.

text.description: The bytes to show as UTF-8 text, hex, base64, base64url and base32, written per from.

name: cipher_encode
title: Convert byte encodings

description: Encrypt text (mode encrypt, the default) or decrypt data (mode decrypt) with AES-GCM (the default), ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-CBC, the key as hex, base64 or base64url. Encrypting without key makes a random 32-byte key and returns it as generated_key, and without nonce a random one is used. The result states its layout (nonce ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag) so other code can read it, and decrypting reads that combined form. Example: key 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f, text hello. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

aad.description: Associated data for aes-gcm and chacha20-poly1305, read per aad_enc: authenticated but not encrypted, so decrypting needs the same.

aad_enc.description: How aad is written: utf8 takes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first.

algo.description: The cipher: aes-gcm or chacha20-poly1305 (authenticated: 12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag), or aes-cbc (unauthenticated: 16-byte IV, PKCS#7 padding) for systems that require it.

data.description: The ciphertext to decrypt (mode decrypt), as base64 or hex: an encrypt's combined output, nonce ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag, or iv ‖ ciphertext for aes-cbc.

data_enc.description: How data is written; auto reads all-hex data as hex and anything else as base64.

enc.description: How text is written: utf8 takes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first.

key.description: The key, read per key_enc: exactly 16, 24 or 32 bytes for AES, 32 for ChaCha20-Poly1305; required to decrypt, while encrypting without one makes a random 32-byte key and returns it as generated_key.

key_enc.description: How key is written; utf8 is refused, because a passphrase is not a key.

nonce.description: The nonce (the IV for aes-cbc) as hex, 12 bytes or 16 for aes-cbc; omit it to encrypt with a random one, or to decrypt data that starts with it.

text.description: The plaintext to encrypt (mode encrypt), read per enc.

name: cipher_encrypt
title: Encrypt or decrypt

description: Hash an input with every common algorithm at once (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE2, Keccak-256, CRC32, Adler-32), each as hex and base64. text is read as UTF-8 unless enc says hex or base64, which is how to hash binary data (up to about 750 KB here); expected is compared with every digest and the result names the algorithm it matches. A trailing newline, CRLF or BOM is flagged, the usual reason two hashes of the same text differ. Example: text abc, expected ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

enc.description: How text is written: utf8 hashes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first, which is how to hash binary data.

expected.description: A checksum to compare with every digest, as hex or base64, bare or labelled (a sha256sum line, sha256=…, SRI's sha384-…); the result names the algorithm it matches.

text.description: The input to hash, read per enc; whitespace and a trailing newline are part of it, and empty input hashes zero bytes.

trim_newline.description: Strip one trailing newline (\n or \r\n) before hashing.

name: cipher_hash
title: Hash text or bytes

description: Compute HMAC-SHA256, SHA-512, SHA-1, MD5 and SHA-3 of text under key at once, or check a webhook signature: expected is compared in constant time with every algorithm, bare or labelled (GitHub's sha256=…, a Stripe-Signature header). For a webhook, text must be the raw request body byte for byte. With key_enc auto the key is read as text and, if expected doesn't match that way, as base64 and hex too, and the result says which reading matched. Example: text {"action":"opened"}, key webhook-secret, expected sha256=…. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

enc.description: How text is written: utf8 takes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first.

expected.description: A MAC to check in constant time against every algorithm, as hex or base64, bare or labelled (GitHub's sha256=…, a Stripe-Signature header).

key.description: The HMAC key, read per key_enc, e.g. a webhook signing secret.

key_enc.description: How key is written: auto reads it as UTF-8 text and, when expected doesn't match that way, tries base64 and hex too and says which reading matched.

text.description: The message, read per enc; for a webhook, the raw request body byte for byte, since re-serialised JSON won't match.

name: cipher_hmac
title: HMAC and webhook signatures

description: Say what a string could be: a hash type with its hashcat mode, a JWT or JWE, a PEM key or certificate, an SSH key, a bcrypt or Argon2 hash, a UUID, an otpauth:// URI, a webhook signature, or base64, hex or base32 data. candidates are ranked by confidence, each with the reason and the cipher.corpberry.com page that reads it. Example: text 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

text.description: The string to identify, up to 1 MiB: a hash, token, key, certificate, password hash, UUID, otpauth:// URI or encoded value; the answer ranks what it could be, with hashcat modes.

name: cipher_identify
title: Identify a string

description: Decode a JWT's header and claims, check exp and nbf against the current time (or now), and verify the signature when key is given: the shared secret for HS*, or a PEM, JWK, JWKS or OpenSSH public key for RS*, PS*, ES* and EdDSA. verification.state says whether the signature checked out, and carries the reason when the key can't be read; validity.state says whether the token is in date. Without a key nothing is verified, since anyone can write a header and payload. Example: token eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9…, key your-256-bit-secret. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

key.description: A key to verify the signature with: the shared secret for HS256/384/512, or a public (or private) key as PEM, JWK, JWKS or an OpenSSH line for RS*, PS*, ES* and EdDSA; omit it to decode without verifying.

key_enc.description: How a shared-secret key is written: auto tries UTF-8 text, base64 and hex and reports which reading verified; ignored for PEM and JWK keys.

leeway.description: Clock skew in seconds allowed when checking exp and nbf.

now.description: Unix time in seconds to use as the current time, e.g. 1700000000; omit it for the real clock.

token.description: The token to decode: a signed JWT (header.payload.signature), or an encrypted JWE of five parts, of which only the header is readable; a Bearer prefix, quotes and line breaks around it are removed.

name: cipher_jwt_decode
title: Decode and verify a JWT

description: Sign a JWT with a shared secret (HS256, the default, HS384 or HS512) or a private key as PEM, JWK or JWKS (RS*, PS*, ES*, EdDSA), optionally adding iat and an exp lifetime. payload and header are JSON text inside a string, and the claims are signed in the order written. The result is the token with the breakdown cipher_jwt_decode gives. Example: key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef, payload {"sub":"42"}, exp 1h. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

alg.description: The signature algorithm: HS* sign with a shared secret, RS* and PS* with an RSA private key, ES256/384/512 with an ECDSA P-256/384/521 private key, EdDSA (or its other name Ed25519) with an Ed25519 private key.

exp.description: A lifetime to add as an exp claim, counted from the current time (or now), unless payload has one; omit it for a token that never expires.

header.description: Extra header members as a JSON object, e.g. {"cty":"JWT"}; alg always comes from alg, and typ defaults to "JWT".

iat.description: Add an iat claim of the current time (or now), unless payload has one.

key.description: The signing key: the shared secret for HS*, or the private key as PEM (PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC 1 or OpenSSH), JWK or JWKS for the others.

key_enc.description: How a shared-secret key is written (signing has no auto); ignored for PEM and JWK keys.

kid.description: A key id: added to the header unless header has one, and used to pick the signing key out of a JWKS.

now.description: Unix time in seconds to use as the current time, e.g. 1700000000; omit it for the real clock.

payload.description: The claims as a JSON object, e.g. {"sub":"42","name":"Ada"}, signed with their order kept.

name: cipher_jwt_sign
title: Sign a JWT

description: Generate a test key pair: Ed25519 (the default), ECDSA on P-256, P-384 or P-521, or RSA of 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits. The result has the private key as PKCS#8 PEM, JWK and OpenSSH, the public key as PEM, JWK and an OpenSSH line, and their fingerprints; with passphrase the private key comes back only as encrypted OpenSSH. Example: type ec-p256, comment ci-deploy-test. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

comment.description: The comment ending the OpenSSH public key line, one printable line of up to 256 characters; default cipher-tools-test-key.

passphrase.description: A passphrase to encrypt the private key with: it then comes back only in OpenSSH format (bcrypt_pbkdf and AES-256-CTR), without the unencrypted PKCS#8 and JWK forms.

type.description: The key pair to generate: Ed25519, ECDSA on P-256, P-384 or P-521, or RSA of 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits (RSA-4096 takes seconds).

name: cipher_keys_generate
title: Generate a key pair

description: Read up to 64 keys and convert each between formats: PEM (PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC 1, SPKI, OpenSSH, or a certificate's key), a JWK or JWKS, or OpenSSH public key lines. Each comes back as PEM, JWK and OpenSSH, with its SPKI and OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprints, its RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, and whether it is private. Example: key ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI… user@host. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

key.description: The key or keys to convert and fingerprint: PEM (PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC 1, SPKI, an OpenSSH private key or a certificate), a JWK or JWKS, or OpenSSH public key lines; up to 64 keys.

name: cipher_keys_inspect
title: Inspect and convert keys

description: Hash a password with bcrypt (the default), Argon2id, scrypt or PBKDF2; each algorithm reads only its own cost fields, bounded so one call stays cheap. The result is the encoded hash a library would store, its parameters read back, and warnings for weak settings such as bcrypt below cost 10. bcrypt refuses a password over 72 bytes instead of silently cutting it. Example: password correct horse battery staple, algo argon2id. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

algo.description: The algorithm; each reads only its own cost fields, and argon2id is what OWASP recommends for new systems.

argon2_m.description: Argon2id's memory in KiB when algo is argon2id, at least 8 per lane, e.g. 19456 (19 MiB, OWASP's minimum with argon2_t 2).

argon2_p.description: Argon2id's lanes (parallelism) when algo is argon2id.

argon2_t.description: Argon2id's passes over its memory when algo is argon2id.

bcrypt_cost.description: bcrypt's cost when algo is bcrypt: 2^cost rounds, each step doubling the time; OWASP's minimum is 10.

password.description: The password to hash, read per password_enc; whitespace is part of it, and bcrypt refuses more than 72 bytes.

password_enc.description: How password is written: utf8 takes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first.

pbkdf2_iterations.description: PBKDF2's iterations when algo is pbkdf2-sha256 or pbkdf2-sha512; the default is OWASP's minimum, 600000 and 210000 respectively.

scrypt_n.description: scrypt's cost N when algo is scrypt: a power of two, and 128 × N × scrypt_r bytes of memory may not pass 128 MiB.

scrypt_p.description: scrypt's parallelism p when algo is scrypt: how many times the memory-hard step runs.

scrypt_r.description: scrypt's block size r when algo is scrypt.

name: cipher_password_hash
title: Hash a password

description: Read a stored password hash (bcrypt, Argon2, scrypt, PBKDF2 including Django's) and check a password against it. state is match or no-match; unchecked when no password is given and the hash's algorithm, parameters and salt are only read; unsupported for a crypt(3) format it names but can't verify; refused for parameters above this server's limits. Example: hash $2b$12$…, password hunter2. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

hash.description: The stored hash to read and check: bcrypt ($2b$…), Argon2 ($argon2id$…), scrypt ($scrypt$…) or PBKDF2 ($pbkdf2-sha256$…, Django's pbkdf2_sha256$…); other crypt(3) formats are named but not verified.

password.description: The password to check against hash, read per password_enc; omit it to only read the hash's algorithm, parameters and salt.

password_enc.description: How password is written: utf8 takes it as typed; hex, base64, base64url or base32 decode it first.

name: cipher_password_verify
title: Check a password hash

description: Generate random values from a cryptographic source: tokens (kind token, the default) as hex, base64url, base64 or letters and digits; passwords from the character sets chosen, with their exact entropy; or UUIDs, version 4 or 7. count makes up to 20 tokens or passwords, or 100 UUIDs, at once. Example: kind password, length 24, sets [lower, upper, digits]. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

bytes.description: Random bytes per token (kind token), e.g. 32 for 256 bits; an alnum token gets enough characters to carry as much entropy.

count.description: How many values to generate: up to 20 tokens or passwords, or up to 100 UUIDs.

exclude_ambiguous.description: Leave out characters easily misread when copied by hand, 0 O 1 l I | and ` (kind password).

format.description: How a token is written (kind token): hex, base64url (URL-safe, unpadded), base64 (padded) or alnum (A-Z, a-z and 0-9).

kind.description: What to generate: token (random bytes, encoded), password (characters from chosen sets) or uuid.

sets.description: The character sets a password draws from (kind password), comma-separated, e.g. lower,upper,digits; each chosen set appears at least once.

version.description: The UUID version (kind uuid): 4 is random; 7 starts with its creation time in milliseconds, readable by anyone who sees it.

name: cipher_random
title: Random tokens, passwords, UUIDs

description: Get the previous, current and next TOTP (or HOTP) code from a base32 secret or a whole otpauth:// URI, with the seconds left in the step. code checks a code within one step either side, and label and issuer build an otpauth:// URI for an authenticator app. now sets the time, to see what the codes were or will be. Example: secret JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP, code 287082. Inputs and outputs pass through corpberry.com and the user's AI provider, so use test material only.

algo.description: The HMAC behind the codes; nearly every authenticator uses SHA1, and Google Authenticator ignores this setting.

code.description: A code to check against the previous, current and next step (or counter).

counter.description: The HOTP counter (mode hotp); codes come back for counter-1, counter and counter+1.

digits.description: Digits per code; most authenticators show 6.

issuer.description: The issuer in the otpauth:// URI the result builds, e.g. Example Corp.

label.description: The account name in the otpauth:// URI the result builds, e.g. alice@example.com.

mode.description: totp for time-based codes (RFC 6238), hotp for counter-based ones (RFC 4226).

now.description: Unix time in seconds to use as the current time, e.g. 1700000000; omit it for the real clock.

secret.description: The shared secret in base32 (any case; spaces, dashes and padding ignored), e.g. JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP, or a whole otpauth:// URI, whose settings then replace every field but code and now.

name: cipher_totp
title: TOTP and HOTP codes
